key_insight: A machine-learning model using linked mother-infant EHR data can estimate gestational age at delivery with high accuracy and good portability across two health systems.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help researchers impute gestational age more reliably in large real-world maternal and neonatal studies when exact pregnancy timing is missing or uncertain.
method: Trained random forest, gradient boosting, and ensemble models on mother-infant EHR data.
Validated the approach at Vanderbilt and replicated it at the University of Michigan.
Compared performance across delivery timing and examined temporal drift in EHR features.
evidence_signal: The ensemble model performed best, reaching ±1 week accuracy of 85.2% at Vanderbilt and 93.1% at Michigan, with MAE of 4.4 and 2.8 days, respectively.
watch_item: Performance was lower for preterm deliveries, so implementation may be less reliable in higher-risk pregnancies or settings with different data patterns.
paper_title: Machine Learning Estimation of Gestational Age at Delivery Using Linked Mother-Infant Electronic Health Records Across Two Health Systems
